title: Turn On Lens Corrections Before You Touch a Slider
excerpt: Every lens bends straight lines and darkens corners, and Lightroom can fix most of that in one click. But the fix only works if the right lens profile is actually selected, and with adapted glass it often is not.

title: Six AI Retouching Myths, Tested on Real Portraits
excerpt: A portrait photographer ran six common objections to AI retouching against real client work: plastic skin, darker skin tones, the cloud, group photos. Most of them failed. But the test was sponsored by the tool being tested, so the method matters more than the verdicts.

title: The Next Sensor Leap Might Be Dynamic Range, Not Megapixels
excerpt: Camera makers keep adding megapixels and autofocus tricks while sales shrink. A sensor design called LOFIC could deliver more than 17 stops of dynamic range, and it is already shipping in a pocket camera.
